verified.title: serve() reaps the vllm child only on the check path; an exception from _write_endpoint_file still orphans the server on the card
verified.evidence:
models/agent_models/service.py:213-232. The guarded block is only the three checks:

    213  proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, env=env)
    214  try:
    215      _wait_healthy(root_url, proc)
    216      _check_model(base_url, row)
    217      _check_render(base_url, row, m, cfg)
    218  except BaseException:
    ...      proc.terminate() ... proc.wait(timeout=60) ... proc.kill()
    227      raise
    228  _write_endpoint_file(
    229      endpoint_path, replica=args.replica, base_url=base_url, host=host, port=args.port,
    230      pid=proc.pid, flags=vars(args), claims=claims, attached_to=None,
    231  )
    232  raise SystemExit(proc.wait())

Lines 228-232 run outside the try. `_write_endpoint_file` (models/agent_models/service.py:83-93) writes `tmp.write_text(...)` then `tmp.replace(path)` into the run directory, which the project rules put on the net disk (/net/tokyo100-10g/...), so it is an ordinary NFS write that can raise OSError. Nothing else owns the child: the only recovery lever the launcher has is `tmux kill-session` (jobs/launch.py:386-388, called from teardown_services jobs/launch.py:493-513 at jobs/launch.py:889,900,911,918). That lever works only while the pane is alive -- tmux signals the pane's process group on kill-session, and vllm is in that group. Once the python parent exits, tee sees EOF, the pane command ends, tmux closes the session without signalling anything, and `teardown_services` finds no session to kill. That is exactly the failure commit 55fb302 was written for ("M-M2 left an orphaned server on tokyo108 card 5"), and .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md:212 records two such sessions still holding tokyo108 cards 0 and 1 after 7 days. For the same reason the normal teardown path is safe (kill-session's group signal reaches vllm directly) -- the hole is only the window where the python parent dies while vllm lives, which lines 228-232 leave open.
verified.scenario: A `sample` launch on tokyo108: `vllm serve gpt-oss-120b` comes up, /health answers, /v1/models names the row, render_ids matches the chat endpoint -- all three checks pass, so the reap handler at line 218 is never entered. Line 228 then writes service_agent_0.json into the run directory on /net/tokyo100-10g and the net mount is briefly unwritable (stale handle, quota, full disk), so `tmp.write_text` raises OSError. The exception leaves serve(), python exits, tee exits, the tmux pane and session close with no signal to the process group, and the 120B vLLM server keeps running and keeps the card's memory. jobs/launch.py sees alive_check fail (no endpoint file) and calls teardown_services, whose `tmux kill-session` reports nothing ended because the session is already gone. The card stays occupied until someone finds the pid by hand -- the same state as M-M2 and as the two 7-day sessions in the errata.
verified.proposed_fix: Own the child for its whole lifetime instead of for the three checks only: move `_write_endpoint_file` and the final `proc.wait()` inside the guarded region, i.e. wrap lines 215-232 in the try and keep the same terminate/wait(60)/kill/wait handler on `except BaseException`. `Popen.terminate()` and `Popen.wait()` on an already-exited process are no-ops, so the normal exit through `raise SystemExit(proc.wait())` passes through the handler harmlessly. A `try/finally` that reaps whenever the child is still alive at the end of serve() expresses the same rule positively: the process started at line 213 is ended before serve() returns by any route.

verdict.reason:
I could not find any guard that closes this window; every step of the finding reproduces from the code.

1. The cited shape is exactly as reported. /home/y-guo/reproduce/new1/models/agent_models/service.py:213 starts the child, 214-227 guard only `_wait_healthy` / `_check_model` / `_check_render`, and the two statements that follow are outside the guard: `_write_endpoint_file(...)` at 228-231 and `raise SystemExit(proc.wait())` at 232. `_write_endpoint_file` (service.py:83-93) does `tmp.write_text(json.dumps(doc))` then `tmp.replace(path)` — a real filesystem write, and `path` is under the run directory, whose root is `/net/tokyo100-10g/data/str01_01/y-guo/reproduce/new1/outputs` (constants/path_outputs.yaml:4; confirmed on live rows, e.g. jobs/runs.jsonl line 41's service piece `--run-dir /net/.../outputs/debug/inject/c96e48a8be3d`). The payload itself cannot raise TypeError (`vars(args)` is str/int/bool/None, `claims = dict(row)` is the YAML-round-tripped frozen row), so the escape route is an OSError from the net-disk write.

2. Nothing else owns the child. The service piece is recorded with `"pid": null` (jobs/runs.jsonl, every `"kind": "service"` entry), and the only end lever for a non-`cpu` piece is `tmux kill-session`: jobs/launch.py:386-389 `_kill_tmux`, used by `teardown_services` (jobs/launch.py:493-513) at jobs/launch.py:889, 900, 911, 918, and by `registry.kill` (jobs/registry.py:1008-1043), whose pid branch applies only to `kind == "cpu"`. 3. That the vLLM child survives its parent here is not theory in this repo, it is measured. Commit 55fb302 ("a refused start ends and reaps the vllm process ... M-M2 left an orphaned server on tokyo108 card 5") is exactly the same exit route — an exception escaping `serve()` after `Popen` succeeded — and it left the 120B server on the card. The wave-3 adjudication had previously rejected that same claim on the argument the reviewer rebuts ("teardown_services tears the service sessions down", .scratch/from-zero/sdd/2026-09-17-wave3/post-merge-review.json item 34), and the 2026-09-20 walk disproved it. .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md:212 records two such sessions holding tokyo108 cards 0 and 1 for 7 days. Neither the errata's fix list (a)-(f) at line 211 nor the seventh fix says anything about the write path, so this is not a ruled-intended behaviour.

Caveat, stated honestly: the trigger is an I/O failure on the net mount (stale handle, quota, full disk), not a deterministic code path — no input makes line 228 raise. What is certain from the code is the ownership hole: between line 228 and the `proc.wait()` of line 232 the process holds a GPU-resident child that no other component can end, and the repo has already paid for that exact hole once.
verdict.corrected_fix:
The direction is right (own the child for its whole lifetime), but prefer the `try/finally` variant the finding mentions second, not the `except BaseException` wrap of lines 215-232. Wrapping the success path in the refusal handler means the normal exit — `raise SystemExit(proc.wait())` — runs `proc.terminate()` on the way out, which reads as "the good path is handled by the failure branch"; the repo rule asks for the rule written once, positively. In models/agent_models/service.py, replace the block at 213-232 with:

    proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, env=env)
    try:
        _wait_healthy(root_url, proc)
        _check_model(base_url, row)
        _check_render(base_url, row, m, cfg)
        _write_endpoint_file(
            endpoint_path, replica=args.replica, base_url=base_url, host=host, port=args.port,
            pid=proc.pid, flags=vars(args), claims=claims, attached_to=None,
        )
        raise SystemExit(proc.wait())
    finally:
        # the vllm process started above is ended before serve() returns by any route:
        # a refused check, a failed endpoint write, or the server's own exit
        if proc.poll() is None:
            proc.terminate()
            try:
                proc.wait(timeout=60)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                proc.kill()
                proc.wait()

This overwrites the partial-ownership logic instead of adding a second special case beside it, keeps the same terminate / wait(60) / kill escalation, and states the condition positively (`proc.poll() is None`, the child is still running). Note the limit, which no code change removes: a SIGHUP or SIGKILL to the python parent skips `finally` entirely — that case is covered because the signal reaches the whole pane process group, vLLM included.

verified.title: Under the new bf16 autocast the packed additive attention mask still goes to the card in float32; the old trainer picked the mask dtype from the autocast flag
verified.evidence:
models/probe_models/base.py:99 is the single place every method's mask reaches the GPU, and it moves device only, never dtype: `attention_mask = batch["attention_mask"].to(device)`. The three methods build that mask in float32 and never cast it: train/methods/ctool.py:122 `attn = torch.full((B, 1, L_pad, L_pad), float("-inf"), dtype=torch.float32)` (also :151-152 `block`/`real`), train/methods/cgen.py:137 and :167-168, train/methods/cparam.py:164 and :194-195. train/utils/trainer.py:71-74 now runs the forward under `torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, enabled=on_card)`, so q/k/v are bfloat16 while this bias stays float32.

The old trainer that commit 0793692 / errata (b) says it is matching did exactly the opposite: legacy/pipeline/train/train_causal_share.py:254 `mask_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if amp else torch.float32` (same line at :563 and :1024) and legacy/pipeline/train/train_causal_share.py:159 `mask = mask.to(dev).to(dtype=mask_dtype)` inside `_forward_packed`, i.e. the mask was shipped in the same dtype the autocast computed in, and the alignment check's float32 pass was the only one that shipped a float32 mask (legacy :800 `_new_forward(new_events, model, dev, torch.float32)` against :837-839 `with torch.autocast(...): _new_forward(new_events, model, dev, torch.bfloat16)`).

The mask is not a small tensor. `_chunk_by_budget` (ctool.py:76-95, cgen.py:89-107, cparam.py:116-134) keeps `n * pad16(L_first) <= budget`, so `B * L_pad <= budget`, and the mask costs `B * L_pad * L_pad * 4` bytes. With schema.py's default `train.max_len = 8192` the train budget is `_TRAIN_BLOCK_MULT * 8192 = 16384` and the validate/predict budget is `_VAL_BLOCK_MULT * 8192 = 32768`. transformers hands a 4-D mask straight through (external/probe-env/.../transformers/masking_utils.py:817-818 "If the mask is already 4D, simply return as-is"), so torch's SDPA receives the float32 bias and materialises its own bfloat16 copy beside the float32 original, which is still held by the batch dict for the whole forward.
verified.scenario: cgen_qwen3_0pt6b / cparam_qwen3_0pt6b at the default train.max_len 8192 on a 48 GB card - the exact configuration fix (b) was made for. A validation block that packs one event of packed_len about 32768 gives L_pad = 32768, B = 1: the additive mask alone is 32768 * 32768 * 4 = 4.3 GB of device memory, and SDPA allocates a further 2.1 GB bfloat16 copy of it while the float32 original is still live. A training block with B = 1, L_pad = 16384 costs 1.07 GB float32 plus a 0.54 GB copy. Under the old trainer's rule the resident mask would have been half that in each case. So between 0.25 GB and 2 GB per block is spent on precision the computation does not use, inside the one forward the version-2 bump exists to make fit; the --debug walks (train.max_steps 20, tiny events) never reached these block sizes, so they could not show it.
verified.proposed_fix: Give the mask the dtype the forward actually computes in, at the one place it crosses onto the card. In `Probe.forward` (models/probe_models/base.py:99), after the `.to(device)`, cast a floating-point mask to the active autocast dtype: `if attention_mask.is_floating_point() and torch.is_autocast_enabled(device.type): attention_mask = attention_mask.to(torch.get_autocast_dtype(device.type))`. Zero and -inf are both exact in bfloat16, so nothing is lost, and the alignment gate keeps its float32 mask automatically because autocast is off there - the same split legacy got from `mask_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if amp else torch.float32`. That edit changes the train stage's numerics, so it carries a `models/probe_models/base.py` VERSION bump with `stale: ("train",)`, which is the bump F2 already asks for.

In `Probe.forward`, replace models/probe_models/base.py:99 with:

    mask = batch["attention_mask"]

The mask holds only 0.0 and -inf (cgen.py:137/167-169 and the same lines in ctool/cparam), both exact in bfloat16, and autocast already hands SDPA a bfloat16 copy of exactly those values (measured: bit-identical output). The train stage's output is unchanged, so the bump rule in base.py:16-25 ("bump only when some existing setting would now produce a different output") does not fire. If F2 asks for a bump on base.py for its own reason, that reason has to carry it; this edit does not.

verified.title: An attach-only agent service piece ends its session on success, and the new session-based DOWN rule reads that as death
verified.evidence: jobs/launch.py:444 `down = (not up) and (not session_ok)` is new in the rewrite (`git diff e3f9cb7..HEAD -- jobs/launch.py`: the old service branch computed only `ok = endpoint_ok and _port_answers(...)` and had no session test). An attach-only piece is a service piece placed on `serving_host` (jobs/launch.py:802-804 `attached = attach is not None and local_i == 0`; `place(...)` returns `serving_host`, models/table.yaml:17-19 `host: tokyo108`, while `login_host: shiga` in constants/path_outputs.yaml:12), and its program writes the endpoint file and returns at once: models/agent_models/service.py:197-207 (`_attach(...)`, `_write_endpoint_file(...)`, `return`). So its tmux session ends by design, seconds after it starts, and from then on `session_ok` is False forever. `up` needs two more things: `endpoint_ok`, a `Path.exists()` on the NFS run directory from the login host (jobs/launch.py:441-442), and `_port_answers`, a TCP connect with a 2-second timeout to the attached server (jobs/launch.py:392-400, 443). Either one failing at a poll after the session has ended latches `down`, and jobs/launch.py:462-463 returns at once; the call site at jobs/launch.py:896-901 then tears the other services down and returns `alive_check`, and run.py:2027-2035 closes the run `launch_failed`. Contract note: contract-errata.md:79 defines a service piece's alive test as "its `service_<kind>_<replica>.json` appears and its port answers" with no session clause, and the new entry (c) at contract-errata.md:211 changes only the window, so this DOWN rule for service pieces is in neither.
verified.scenario: A second `inject` run against the vLLM server a live `sample` run already holds: `_find_attach_target` matches (jobs/launch.py:757-758), so piece 0 is attach-only on tokyo108. alive_check stats `<run_dir>/service_agent_0.json` from shiga at t=0, 5, 10, 15 s and each miss caches a negative lookup for that NFS directory; the remote process writes the file and exits at t=18 s. At the t=20 s poll `registry.live_sessions()` already reports the session gone while the login host has not yet seen the new directory entry, so `up` is False and `session_ok` is False: `down` fires, alive_check returns immediately, `teardown_services` kills the probe service that did come up, and the run is closed `launch_failed` although nothing was wrong. The same latch fires when the endpoint file is visible but the attached server, busy serving the other run's six loop pieces, does not complete a TCP connect inside the 2-second probe. The old code simply polled again and passed on the next poll.
verified.proposed_fix: Judge a service piece down by what it failed to produce, not by its session: `down = (not endpoint_ok) and (not session_ok)` — a service piece is down when its session has ended and it never wrote its endpoint file. A real server writes its endpoint only after `/health` answers, so this keeps the real-death case; an attach-only piece that wrote its endpoint and exited stays out of the down state and reaches `up` on the poll where the port answers.

The finding holds; I could find no guard, caller or ruling that prevents it.

2. models/agent_models/service.py:197-207 — under `--attach-only` the program runs `_attach(...)`, `_write_endpoint_file(...)`, `return`. It is the only service program that returns on success; models/probe_models/service.py:181-185 writes its endpoint file and then calls `server.serve_forever()`. So exactly one piece shape ends its tmux session as its success state.

3. The attach-only piece is an ordinary tmux piece in the alive check: jobs/launch.py:802-804 sets `attached`, `place()` (jobs/launch.py:285-287) returns `serving_host`, the piece is appended with `kind: "service"` (jobs/launch.py:817) and therefore lands in `service_pieces` at jobs/launch.py:893-899. `_start_tmux` (jobs/launch.py:381-384) uses a plain `tmux new-session -d`, so the session dies with the command. Consequences are as reported: `teardown_services` (jobs/launch.py:493-513) is skipped only when this run's id is in someone else's `attached_to` — the attaching run is the other side of that relation, so it runs and kills its own probe service — and run.py:2029-2033 appends `status: "launch_failed"`.

4. The state is reached in a real run, not only in theory. jobs/runs.jsonl:71 is `inject-7c45d0327b85`, launched at commit 8c72466 (c470bd1 is its ancestor), piece 1 = `--attach-only --attached-to inject-ecf0f0957791` on tokyo108. Timestamps in /net/tokyo100-10g/data/str01_01/y-guo/reproduce/new1/outputs/debug/inject/7c45d0327b85/: meta.json 15:27:20.83 (lock released, tmux starts), log/1.txt 15:27:21.90, service_agent_0.json 15:27:22.16, service_probe_0.json 15:27:34.60, done.json 15:31:12. The attach piece's session was gone ~1.3 s after it started, and alive_check kept polling ~12 s more waiting for the probe service; every one of those polls evaluated `down = (not up) and (not session_ok)` with `session_ok` permanently False. A single stale `Path.exists()` or one missed 2 s TCP connect at any of them closes the run. The piece has no `waiting` state and no retry at all — that part is provable from the code alone.

5. The visibility lag the scenario needs is available on this machine: /proc/mounts has `tokyo100-10g:/data/str01_01 ... nfs4 vers=4.0 ... rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime` — no `noac`, no `actimeo=`, no `lookupcache=`, so Linux defaults (acdirmin 30 / acdirmax 60) apply and a negative lookup cached at one poll is trusted for tens of seconds. The login host wrote meta.json into that directory itself just before, which sets the directory attribute timeout fresh. Session state is read live over `ssh tmux ls` and is never stale, so the observer can hold a fresh "session gone" against a cached "no endpoint file". With a cold remote interpreter (errata (c) records a 42 s first log line on tokyo108) the miss is cached at poll 1, the file lands, the session ends, and the next poll latches `down`.

One correction to the finding: its contract note is partly wrong. Errata line 79 has no session clause, but entry (c) at contract-errata.md:211 does say "each piece is up, down (session ended, or a `Traceback`) or waiting", so the rule as written does cover service pieces. What no ruling covers is the piece whose ended session means success.
verdict.corrected_fix:
The proposed `down = (not endpoint_ok) and (not session_ok)` is wrong and must not be taken: the endpoint file is never removed, so a real vLLM service that wrote its endpoint and then died would never be judged down — the check would spin to `launch_timeout_s` = 1800 s (jobs/registry.py:41) before reporting failure, discarding the fast-death detection fix (c) was written for. It is also a double negative.

Root cause to overwrite: the DOWN rule compares two facts of different freshness as if they were simultaneous — a live `ssh tmux ls` reading against a directory lookup that this host's NFS client can serve from cache for tens of seconds — and it assumes every service piece holds its session for its whole life, which the attach-only agent piece does not.

Right rule, replacing the service branch's death test in jobs/launch.py:440-443 (no per-piece exemption, one condition, applied to every service piece):

    SESSION_END_GRACE_S = 60      # module constant, the acdirmax of the outputs mount

    # inside alive_check, before the loop:
    session_gone_at: dict[int, float] = {}
    ...
    if p.get("kind") == "service":
        run_dir = p.get("run_dir")
        endpoint_ok = bool(run_dir) and (Path(run_dir) / p["endpoint_file"]).exists()
        up = endpoint_ok and _port_answers(p.get("host"), p.get("port"))
        # A service piece's evidence is its endpoint file and an answering port, and that
        # evidence arrives through this host's directory cache, which can lag a write made
        # on the serving host. An `--attach-only` agent piece writes its endpoint file and
        # returns (models/agent_models/service.py serve --attach-only), so its ended session
        # is its success state. A service piece is down when its session has ended and it
        # still owes its evidence one grace period later.
        if up:
            session_gone_at.pop(p["index"], None)
            down = False
        elif session_ok:
            session_gone_at.pop(p["index"], None)
            down = False
        else:
            first_seen_gone = session_gone_at.setdefault(p["index"], time.time())
            down = time.time() - first_seen_gone >= SESSION_END_GRACE_S

This keeps every property fix (c) bought: a service whose session ends without ever producing its evidence is still declared down, now after one grace period instead of instantly (60 s out of an 1800 s budget), and a refused attach-only piece — which writes no endpoint file — is still caught. A successful attach-only piece reaches `up` on the poll where its endpoint file becomes visible, and a single stale lookup or one slow TCP connect no longer ends the run. verified.title: probe_eval dereferences referenced_run_dir's None for the referenced eval's train run
verified.evidence: eval/utils/probe_eval.py:599-600 — `ref_train_dir = schema.referenced_run_dir("train", ref_train_key)` followed immediately by `ref_train_meta = json.loads((ref_train_dir / "meta.json").read_text())`. `referenced_run_dir` is declared `Path | None` and returns None when neither root holds the key (experimental_settings/schema.py:1360-1378). The sibling lookup twelve lines up does handle it: `if ref_eval_dir is None or not (ref_eval_dir / "done.json").exists(): raise ValueError(...)` (eval/utils/probe_eval.py:586-590). `ref_train_key` is read out of the *referenced* eval's `meta.json` (line 598), so it is not in this eval's own upstream map and run.py's `_refuse_missing_upstream` (run.py:1826-1838), which is the guard that covers the other three callers, never sees it.
verified.scenario: A generator eval's `eval.theta_from` names a classifier eval that was pinned by the `dir:` form (contracts 5.4's case for a directory made before this scheme). That eval's `meta.json` names train key `a1b2c3d4e5f6`, whose directory has since been cleaned off the net disk. `referenced_run_dir` finds it under neither root and returns None, and line 600 raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'NoneType' and 'str'`; the eval piece dies with that traceback instead of the named refusal the ref_eval_dir branch gives for the same class of miss, and the operator has to read the traceback to learn which key is missing.
verified.proposed_fix: Write the same positive check the ref_eval_dir branch uses, right after line 599: when `ref_train_dir` is a directory holding `meta.json`, go on; otherwise raise `ValueError(f"train key {ref_train_key} of the referenced classifier eval {ref_eval_dir}: no run directory under either root")`.

verdict.reason:
I could not find a guard, and the code path reproduces end to end.

Reachability of the None. `schema.referenced_run_dir` returns None when neither root holds the key (experimental_settings/schema.py:1371-1378: two candidates, `settings.yaml` match first, then `is_dir()`, then `return None`). At eval/utils/probe_eval.py:599-600 the returned value is used with no check: `ref_train_dir = schema.referenced_run_dir("train", ref_train_key)` then `json.loads((ref_train_dir / "meta.json").read_text())`. With None that is `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'NoneType' and 'str'`, and probe_eval has no handler (eval/utils/probe_eval.py:662-672: `main` calls `run` directly under `__main__`), so the eval piece dies on a traceback that names neither the key nor a path.

No guard upstream. The eval stage's upstream table holds exactly two entries, `train` (source `same`) and `theta_from.eval` (source `ref:eval.theta_from`, only for a generator method) — experimental_settings/schema.py:250-252. run.py's pre-launch refusal walks only that map (run.py:1998-1999 calling `_upstream_dirs`/`_refuse_missing_upstream`, run.py:1826-1838), so it covers `theta_from.eval` but never the *referenced* eval's own train key, which is read out of the referenced run's `meta.json` at eval/utils/probe_eval.py:597-598. That is why the other three `referenced_run_dir` callers are safe — eval/score_run.py:182 (`baseline.sample`) and jobs/launch.py:838-839 (`probe_score.train`, `probe_gen.train`) all take keys that are in the launched stage's own upstream map and have already passed run.py:1826-1838.

Nothing between lines 586 and 600 touches the referenced eval's train directory: 587-590 checks only `ref_eval_dir/done.json`, 591 `read_report` reads files inside the eval directory, 597 reads the eval directory's `meta.json`. So reaching 600 with None needs only a generator eval whose referenced classifier eval directory is intact while that eval's train directory is gone from both roots — a train directory is where `predictions.parquet` lives, so it is the plausible cleaning target.

No contract or errata ruling covers it. Contracts 5.4 (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:3296-3314) says only that "`run.py` refuses to start a stage whose referenced run has no `done.json`" — the referenced eval's train run is not a reference of this setting, so 5.4 does not reach it. Errata entry (e) (.scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md, last-but-one entry) says only that the four sites switch to one function; it states no policy that the caller may skip the None.

It is a regression of that very fix. `git diff e3f9cb7..HEAD -- eval/utils/probe_eval.py` (commit 08337dc) changed both lines from `schema.run_dir_of(..., debug=False)` to `schema.referenced_run_dir(...)`. The sibling at 586 gained `ref_eval_dir is None or ...`; line 599 did not. Before the change, a missing train directory gave `FileNotFoundError: <root>/train/<key>/meta.json`, which at least names the missing key; after it, the message names nothing.

One caveat on the reviewer's wording, which does not affect the verdict: their scenario picks the `dir:` form pinned at a directory "made before this scheme", and such a directory may carry no current-format `meta.json`, in which case line 598 (`ref_meta["upstream"]["train"]`) raises KeyError before line 600 is reached. The defect stands unchanged for the name form and the `key:` form, where the referenced eval's `meta.json` is current and only its train directory is missing.
verdict.corrected_fix:
The proposed fix is acceptable in shape — it overwrites "assume the lookup answered" with "use the directory the lookup found, otherwise refuse by name", which is the right logic, not a special case bolted beside a wrong one. Two adjustments:

1. Write the condition positively and let the message name where it looked, the way run.py:1832-1836 does, so the operator does not have to guess which root was searched. Replacing lines 599-600 with:

```python
ref_train_dir = schema.referenced_run_dir("train", ref_train_key)
if ref_train_dir is not None and (ref_train_dir / "meta.json").exists():
    ref_train_meta = json.loads((ref_train_dir / "meta.json").read_text())
else:
    raise ValueError(
        f"train key {ref_train_key} of the referenced classifier eval {ref_eval_dir}: "
        f"no run directory holding meta.json under either root")
```

2. The sibling guard at eval/utils/probe_eval.py:587 is itself written as a double negative (`if ref_eval_dir is None or not (ref_eval_dir / "done.json").exists()`). If the owner wants the positive-form rule applied consistently in this function, flip that one the same way (`if ref_eval_dir is not None and (ref_eval_dir / "done.json").exists(): ... else: raise`) in the same edit, rather than copying the negative shape into the new guard.

refuted.title: Probe.generate's GENERATE_BATCH change altered a train-stage output with no VERSION bump, so two different generate implementations share one train key
refuted.reason:
The finding's concrete scenario rests on a premise that is false on disk and in the ledger, and its closing claim about the ledger is false too.

1) The cited run directory's best/ was written by the BATCHED generate, not before it. /net/tokyo100-10g/data/str01_01/y-guo/reproduce/new1/outputs/debug/train/5b398c217e13/train_done.json reads {"key": "5b398c217e13", "commit": "44a1eb8", ...} and the same directory's train_log.jsonl start row reads "commit": "44a1eb8"; best/ and train_done.json are both dated 09-20 06:23, while 44a1eb8 (the GENERATE_BATCH commit) is dated 09-20 06:18 (git log). The sibling generator run is the same: .../train/b45633250e8b/train_done.json reads "commit": "44a1eb8". So the val_params_all_ok = 0.453125 that picked best/ (train_log.jsonl eval row) was decoded in GENERATE_BATCH shape, and the predict-only relaunch at jobs/runs.jsonl line 61 (2026-09-20 15:04, commit 8c72466) wrote predictions.parquet with the same batched generate on top of it. The mixed state the scenario describes did not occur and is not on disk.

2) No single-call-generate run could ever have left a best/. train/utils/trainer.py:267-278: _validate_and_maybe_save calls metrics = method.validate(...) at :271 and only then probe.save(best_dir, ...) at :277, so best/ appears only after validate returns. validate is exactly where the single-call generate died: 44a1eb8's commit message records that one call over the whole validation frame ran cgen b45633250e8b and cparam 5b398c217e13 --debug out of memory. jobs/runs.jsonl lines 17 and 18 are the only two generator train starts ever recorded at commit 0793692 (single-call generate), and neither has a successful finish; the finished generator rows are lines 49 and 52 (06:52) and 64 (15:18), all at 44a1eb8 or later.

3) Nothing older is reachable anyway. 0793692 (06:12) bumped train/utils/trainer.py to VERSION 2 with stale ("train",) — six minutes before 44a1eb8 — and train/utils/trainer.py is the first entry of STAGES["train"]["versions"] (experimental_settings/schema.py:243-245), so every train key moved then. The only window in which a run directory under a current key could hold single-call-generate output is 06:12-06:18, and the two generator launches in it (lines 17, 18) crashed.

4) "Nothing in the ledger can separate the two code states" is wrong. Every start row carries commit: jobs/runs.jsonl line 18 = 0793692, line 23 = 44a1eb8, line 61 = 8c72466 (parsed from the file). The checkpoint side records it too — train_done.json and train_log.jsonl both carry "commit" — and .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md line 166 states this is the design: "_versions in settings.yaml and meta.json keeps recording the file's real VERSION (with _commit, the record of which program made the output)".

5) The rule is not violated as written. models/probe_models/base.py:15-19 says "Bump VERSION only when some existing setting would now produce a different output" — a necessary condition on bumping, not an obligation to bump; and the ruling behind it (contract-errata.md line 166, gyb 2026-09-18) states the purpose as "the outputs that matter are the ones a large model produced: sample, train, inject; a bump must never silently cost them", with stale defined as "the stages whose existing outputs can no longer be used". Here there are no such outputs to invalidate, which is what errata entry (d) means by "no generator train run had ever finished".

The proposed fix would also cause the loss the rule exists to prevent: a stale ("train",) bump re-keys the train stage for every method, including ctool, whose PROBE_KIND = "classifier" (train/methods/ctool.py:26) and which never calls Probe.generate, discarding the finished ctool train run (jobs/runs.jsonl line 67) and the evals and inject runs pinned to those train keys, in exchange for invalidating nothing the single-call generate ever produced.

refuted.title: The errata's definition of the alive check still says 30 seconds and gives a service piece no session clause, so the rewrite contradicts it
refuted.reason:
The finding treats `.scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md` as a document that must hold one current definition per topic. The file's own stated contract and its whole history say the opposite, and the two things the finding says are missing are in fact written at line 211.

1. The file is an append-only record whose later entry supersedes an earlier one by quoting it, never by editing it. Its header (.scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md:1-7) says "The contracts document is never edited; this file records what the build does instead", with the per-entry format `- <contracts section>: <what it says> -> <what the build does>` — every entry is a delta against a prior statement, so a superseding entry is the file's normal shape, not a contradiction. `git log --numstat -- .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md` shows 18 commits, of which 17 add lines and delete none; the single 1-add/1-delete commit (62d9b12) is the owner amending the ruling entry they had added hours earlier in 3ea9c0b, not a rewrite of a ruling that an implementation had already superseded.

2. Superseding-by-back-reference is the established convention, applied by owner rulings: contract-errata.md:181 heads itself `0.2 / 2.1 / 2.6 (eval/methods/, the ruling entry above marked "Not done yet")` and contract-errata.md:184 heads itself `3.3 / 8.6 (the ruling entry above, "what a VERSION bump invalidates")`; both override the earlier entry and leave its text untouched. contract-errata.md:183 states the rule outright: "Ticket 11, the wave-4 records and the errata entries above keep the old names as history." Fix (c) follows exactly that convention — it is headed `8.1 (alive_check, "never defined")`, quoting line 79's own words ("an alive check is named and never defined") and naming the same contracts section 8.1. So the link the finding says a reader cannot make is printed in the entry's first four words.

3. The finding's claim that the new entry "says nothing about a service piece" is false as written. contract-errata.md:211 fix (c) says "**each** piece is up, down (session ended, or a `Traceback`) or waiting". "each piece" covers the service kind; the `Traceback` alternative is the only kind-specific one (a service piece has no log test at line 79 either), so for a service piece the down rule reduces to "session ended" — which is precisely jobs/launch.py:444, `down = (not up) and (not session_ok)`. The code's non-service branch (jobs/launch.py:456, `down = has_traceback or (not session_ok)`) is the same rule with the `(not up)` conjunct dropped as redundant, since `up` at jobs/launch.py:455 already requires `session_ok and not has_traceback`. There is no rule at jobs/launch.py:444 that entry (c) fails to license.

4. The finding's claim that the 30 s window is left uncorrected is also false. contract-errata.md:211 names the 30-second window as the defect ("a fixed 30-second window closed a train run `launch_failed` whose first log line came after 42 s on tokyo108") and states the replacement bound ("the check returns on all up, on the first down, or at `launch_timeout_s`") for the whole check, not for one kind; line 79 already bounded the service piece by `DEFAULTS["launch_timeout_s"]`, so after (c) one bound governs every kind. jobs/launch.py:424-425 implements it (`window_s = registry.DEFAULTS["launch_timeout_s"]`). The proposed fix's substance ("the window is `launch_timeout_s` for every kind") is therefore already in the file.

5. "Line 79 is still the only full definition" is false in a second way: jobs/launch.py:408-421 carries the complete definition in `alive_check`'s docstring — the three states, the 4 KB tail, the default window, the service piece's endpoint-file-plus-port test — and cites the errata section it implements.

What the finding would cost: its proposed fix asks an agent to rewrite an errata entry that records what the build did up to 2026-09-20, which erases why `launch_timeout_s` replaced 30 s and breaks the convention ruled at contract-errata.md:183. The repo rule the task cites ("a fix overwrites the wrong logic; no special case beside it") is about code logic; nothing in it makes a dated record's superseded entry a defect. No behaviour goes wrong in the finding's scenario — the reader it describes lands on an entry headed with the exact section number and quoted words of the entry it replaces.
